'''Jordan Alan Gross''' (born July 20, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Carolina Panthers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. '''Jordan Russell Kent''' (born July 24, 1984) is an American sports broadcaster for [[CBS Sports Network]] where he calls play-by-play for college basketball, football, [[NBA]] and [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]]. Jordan is a former [[American football]] [[wide receiver]], television [[Play-by-play|play-by-play]] announcer for the [[Golden State Valkyries]] on [[KPIX]] (also [[KPYX]]) and former television [[play-by-play]] announcer for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on [[NBC Sports Northwest]].  Jordan is the executive producer for Talkin' Ducks, on networks throughout Oregon. During the 2020 NBA Bubble, Jordan called Blazer games on the heels of the resignation of [[Kevin Calabro]]. Jordan frequently works with [[Nintendo]] of America covering high level gaming tournaments which have been featured on [[TNT (American TV network)|TNT]] and the [[Disney Channel|Disney]] channel. Jordan was drafted by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the sixth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]] after he began playing football when he was a junior in college at the University of Oregon.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> While at the [[University of Oregon]], Jordan also played Basketball and ran Track, making him the first three-sport college athlete at the University of Oregon since World War II. Since 2012, Jordan has operated award-winning youth sport camps throughout Oregon and Washington called Jordan Kent's Just Kids Skill Camps.<ref>https://jordankentcamps.com/ Jordan Kent's Just Kids Skill Camps</ref>

'''Jordan Shea Rashad Norwood''' (born September 29, 1986)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jordan Norwood Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NorwJo00.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004174053/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NorwJo00.htm |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=March 11, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[punt returner]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After playing [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], he was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2009. Norwood also became a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Denver Broncos]] throughout his career. During [[Super Bowl 50]], Norwood set a then-Super Bowl record with a 61-yard punt return—the longest in Super Bowl history at the time—which stood until [[Kadarius Toney]]'s 65-yard punt return during [[Super Bowl LVII]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swanson |first=Ben |date=February 2, 2021 |title=Five from 50: How Jordan Norwood made the most of a fragile moment and set a Super Bowl record |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/five-from-50-jordan-norwood-super-bowl-record-punt-return-interview |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Denver Broncos}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Longest punt return in a Super Bowl game |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/648540-longest-punt-return-in-a-super-bowl-game |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Guinness World Records}}</ref>

Norwood is the son of [[Brian Norwood]], the current assistant coach for safeties at [[TCU Horned Frogs football|Texas Christian University (TCU)]], and younger brother of [[Gabe Norwood]], a professional basketball player for the [[Rain or Shine Elasto Painters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA).
